needs.title: A safe place tonight
needs.recognise: Sleeping outside, staying somewhere unsafe, or having nowhere to stay.
needs.first_action: Start with the direct local accommodation contacts below and Central Intake online. Ask about today, who can stay, cost and transport. If children or a young person are involved, also use the youth and family section.

needs.title: A home for the longer term
needs.recognise: Overcrowding, unsuitable housing, repeated temporary stays or needing supported housing.
needs.first_action: Ask for help to apply for housing and to keep documents and contact details up to date. A housing application or priority approval does not secure accommodation tonight.

needs.title: Keeping a tenancy
needs.recognise: Rent arrears, an eviction notice, repairs, a bond dispute or a tenancy at risk.
needs.first_action: Seek tenancy advice early. Give the date on any notice or hearing. Ask a financial counsellor about debts while a housing worker helps protect the tenancy.

needs.title: Food and everyday essentials
needs.recognise: A meal, food vouchers, clothing, washing, showers or a place to contact a worker.
needs.first_action: Use a day centre or relief service in your area. Opening times and stock differ. A day centre can help you contact other services; it does not necessarily provide overnight accommodation.

needs.title: Income bills and debt
needs.recognise: No income, problems with payments, debts or unaffordable bills.
needs.first_action: Ask for payment or financial counselling help. Explain any urgent deadline and missing documents. Do not wait for a housing placement before seeking income support.

needs.title: ID phones and online access
needs.recognise: Missing identification, no reliable phone, no email or trouble using online services.
needs.first_action: Tell a worker what you have and what is missing. Ask for help with paper or in-person routes, safe mail collection, and a reliable way to stay in contact.

needs.title: Safety from violence
needs.recognise: Domestic, family or sexual violence, threats or an unsafe place to stay.
needs.first_action: Immediate danger: call 000. Otherwise use a local specialist service or 1800RESPECT. Agree on a safe contact method and explain who must not be told your location.

needs.title: Physical and mental health
needs.recognise: Illness, distress, medication, a health check or urgent mental health support.
needs.first_action: Critical or life-threatening symptoms: call 000. For other needs use a community clinic, healthdirect or a mental health service. Ask about transport and an interpreter.

needs.title: Alcohol and other drugs
needs.recognise: Advice, withdrawal support, treatment or help to reduce harm.
needs.first_action: Contact an alcohol and other drugs service to discuss a safe next step. Tell the worker about your housing situation and any medical concerns. Residential treatment requires separate assessment and availability.

needs.title: Children young people and families
needs.recognise: Youth accommodation, family support, school continuity, counselling or child safety.
needs.first_action: A young person or family can ask for housing help without first proving a special label. Accommodation age and family rules differ. Ask how children can stay safe and remain connected with school and support.

needs.title: Legal help and leaving care
needs.recognise: Legal problems or planning to leave prison, hospital, out-of-home care or another service.
needs.first_action: Start planning before release or discharge when possible. Ask for a named worker and a confirmed place to go, medication, ID, income, transport and follow-up. Do not treat a referral as acceptance.

needs.title: Language culture disability and care
needs.recognise: Interpreting, disability support, older-person care, community connection or difficult travel.
needs.first_action: Ask for the language, cultural support or accessibility you need. Keep ordinary housing and essential-support pathways open while an assessment or disability application is underway.
